question: According to Titus 1:2, upon what divine attribute and ancient promise is the Christian faith grounded?
opt1: In hope of eternal life, which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began
opt2: In hope of earthly riches, which the Roman emperor guaranteed to faithful subjects
opt3: In hope of military victory, which Jewish zealots prophesied in the wilderness
opt4: In hope of philosophical enlightenment, which Greek scholars recorded in academies
correct: In hope of eternal life, which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began
explanation: Paul establishes that Christian hope rests on the veracity of the immutable God who cannot lie, who promised eternal life before creation. Titus 1:2 (KJV) - "In hope of eternal life, which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began;"

question: In Titus 1:4, how does Paul address Titus in the salutation of the epistle?
opt1: To Titus, a royal ambassador of the Roman Senate
opt2: To Titus, mine own son after the common faith
opt3: To Titus, an honored scribe of the Jerusalem temple
opt4: To Titus, a master philosopher of Corinth
correct: To Titus, mine own son after the common faith
explanation: Paul greets Titus with spiritual intimacy, designating him as his genuine spiritual child sharing the common apostolic faith. Titus 1:4 (KJV) - "To Titus, mine own son after the common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Saviour."

question: According to Titus 1:5, why did Paul leave Titus on the island of Crete?
opt1: That thou shouldest oversee commercial shipping and collect taxes for Rome
opt2: That thou shouldest build a central temple of stone in the capital city
opt3: That thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city
opt4: That thou shouldest establish philosophical academies to debate Cretan poets
correct: That thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city
explanation: Titus was stationed in Crete to complete unfinished ecclesiastical organization and establish qualified pastoral leadership across Cretan congregations. Titus 1:5 (KJV) - "For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee:"

question: In Titus 1:6, what domestic qualification regarding children is required of a candidate for elder?
opt1: Having children who hold civil office in Roman municipal administration
opt2: Having children who have memorized the entire oral law of the Pharisees
opt3: Having children who have taken vows of perpetual poverty and monastic silence
opt4: Having faithful children not accused of riot or unruly
correct: Having faithful children not accused of riot or unruly
explanation: An elder candidate's family life must exhibit orderly, faithful governance, with believing children free from accusations of reckless living or rebellion. Titus 1:6 (KJV) - "If any be blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children not accused of riot or unruly."

question: According to Titus 1:7-8, as the steward of God, what negative vices must a bishop avoid, and what positive virtues must he embody?
opt1: Not selfwilled, not soon angry, not given to wine, no striker, not given to filthy lucre; but a lover of hospitality, a lover of good men, sober, just, holy, temperate
opt2: Not poor, not uneducated, not humble, no merchant, not given to manual labor; but proud, wealthy, eloquent, and commanding
opt3: Not married, not sociable, not eating meat, no speaker, not given to secular trade; but solitary, ascetic, austere, and silent
opt4: Not obedient to civil magistrates, not paying taxes, not eating with Gentiles, no courier; but legalistic, zealous for circumcision, and strict
correct: Not selfwilled, not soon angry, not given to wine, no striker, not given to filthy lucre; but a lover of hospitality, a lover of good men, sober, just, holy, temperate
explanation: As God's household steward, an overseer must be free from arrogance, quick temper, drunkenness, violence, and greed, displaying instead hospitality, goodness, justice, holiness, and self-restraint. Titus 1:7-8 (KJV) - "For a bishop must be blameless, as the steward of God; not selfwilled, not soon angry, not given to wine, no striker, not given to filthy lucre; But a lover of hospitality, a lover of good men, sober, just, holy, temperate;"

question: In Titus 1:9, what doctrinal steadfastness is demanded of an elder, and for what dual pastoral purpose?
opt1: Studying Greek rhetoric and pagan mythology, that he may be able to entertain crowds in civic theaters
opt2: Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers
opt3: Memorizing ancestral genealogies, that he may establish Levitical heritage before civil courts
opt4: Revising apostolic teaching, that he may appease Roman magistrates and prevent lawsuits
correct: Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers
explanation: The overseer must cling tenaciously to orthodox apostolic teaching so he can encourage the faithful and refute theological opponents. Titus 1:9 (KJV) - "Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers."

question: According to Titus 1:10-11, who were the unruly deceivers subverting whole houses, and what was their corrupt motivation?
opt1: Roman soldiers demanding quarterly tax registers for the emperor
opt2: Athenian philosophers advocating stoic indifference in market squares
opt3: Specially they of the circumcision, whose mouths must be stopped, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre's sake
opt4: Egyptian merchants seeking exclusive trading monopolies in Cretan ports
correct: Specially they of the circumcision, whose mouths must be stopped, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre's sake
explanation: Judaizing false teachers were disrupting whole households with unauthorized legalistic doctrines driven by sordid financial gain. Titus 1:10-11 (KJV) - "For there are many unruly and vain talkers and deceivers, specially they of the circumcision: Whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for filthy lucre's sake."

question: In Titus 1:12-13, what famous cultural proverb from a Cretan prophet does Paul cite, and what pastoral response does he mandate?
opt1: The Cretians are noble warriors, wise philosophers, true friends; wherefore honor them with civic garlands
opt2: The Cretians are skilled navigators, wealthy merchants, builders of cities; wherefore praise their industries
opt3: The Cretians are devout worshipers of Jupiter, observers of sacred omens; wherefore compromise with their temples
opt4: The Cretians are alway liars, evil beasts, slow bellies; wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith
correct: The Cretians are alway liars, evil beasts, slow bellies; wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith
explanation: Paul quotes the Cretan poet Epimenides regarding the degenerate moral reputation of the islanders, directing Titus to administer sharp rebuke to restore theological and moral health. Titus 1:12-13 (KJV) - "One of themselves, even a prophet of their own, said, The Cretians are alway liars, evil beasts, slow bellies. This witness is true. Wherefore rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith;"

question: According to Titus 1:14, what two harmful corruptions must Cretan believers avoid paying heed to?
opt1: Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth
opt2: Roman imperial decrees, and municipal court summons
opt3: Egyptian astronomical calendars, and Babylonian planetary charts
opt4: Greek athletic regulations, and Olympic crowns
correct: Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth
explanation: Believers are commanded to reject unscriptural Jewish myths and man-made ascetic legalisms that deflect the soul from divine truth. Titus 1:14 (KJV) - "Not giving heed to Jewish fables, and commandments of men, that turn from the truth."

question: In Titus 1:15, what profound contrast does Paul draw regarding the perception of all things between the pure and the defiled?
opt1: Unto the rich all goods are lawful: but unto the poor all food is unclean and forbidden
opt2: Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled
opt3: Unto the ascetic all physical pleasures are demonic: but unto the worldly all sins are harmless
opt4: Unto the Jew ceremonial washings grant life: but unto the Gentile circumcision brings condemnation
correct: Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled
explanation: Internal moral purity sanctifies external things, whereas an unbelieving and polluted heart contaminates even the mind and conscience. Titus 1:15 (KJV) - "Unto the pure all things are pure: but unto them that are defiled and unbelieving is nothing pure; but even their mind and conscience is defiled."

question: In Titus 2:2, what six godly character traits are prescribed for the aged men in the church?
opt1: That the aged men be wealthy, commanding, proud, swift to speak, fond of luxury, severe in discipline
opt2: That the aged men be silent, solitary, withdrawn from public gatherings, fasting daily, avoiding youth
opt3: That the aged men be sober, grave, temperate, sound in faith, in charity, in patience
opt4: That the aged men be argumentative, zealous for Jewish genealogies, demanding double tribute, governing courts
correct: That the aged men be sober, grave, temperate, sound in faith, in charity, in patience
explanation: Older Christian men are exhorted to exhibit dignity, self-control, balance, and soundness in faith, love, and endurance. Titus 2:2 (KJV) - "That the aged men be sober, grave, temperate, sound in faith, in charity, in patience."

question: According to Titus 2:3, how must aged women conduct themselves, and what role are they called to fulfill?
opt1: In ostentatious apparel displaying church riches, presiding over elder councils, managing finances
opt2: In solitary monastic vows, refusing interaction with family, spending life in silence
opt3: In public political lobbying, contesting municipal court decrees, demanding civic honors
opt4: In behaviour as becometh holiness, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teachers of good things
correct: In behaviour as becometh holiness, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teachers of good things
explanation: Older women are called to reverent holiness, avoiding slander and excess, and serving as mentors who teach what is good. Titus 2:3 (KJV) - "The aged women likewise, that they be in behaviour as becometh holiness, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teachers of good things;"

question: In Titus 2:4-5, what are the aged women instructed to teach the young women, and for what supreme spiritual reason?
opt1: To love their husbands, to love their children, to be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed
opt2: To pursue public political careers, neglect domestic duties, demand equal authority over elders, that the church appear modern
opt3: To take vows of perpetual celibacy, abandon household responsibilities, wander from house to house, that they may fast
opt4: To master Greek philosophy, debate in civic market squares, challenge Roman magistrates, that they may gain fame
correct: To love their husbands, to love their children, to be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed
explanation: Young wives are to be mentored in domestic love, purity, diligence at home, and marital respect, ensuring that God's Word is never discredited by disorderly conduct. Titus 2:4-5 (KJV) - "That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed."

question: According to Titus 2:6-7, what is the single primary exhortation given to young men, and how is Titus himself to model it?
opt1: Young men exhort to amass wealth; in all things shewing thyself an ambitious merchant: in doctrine compromise
opt2: Young men likewise exhort to be sober minded; in all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity
opt3: Young men exhort to seek military honors; in all things shewing thyself a skilled fighter: in speech defiance
opt4: Young men exhort to debate philosophers; in all things shewing thyself an orator: in doctrine novelty
correct: Young men likewise exhort to be sober minded; in all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity
explanation: Young men must cultivate self-control (sober-mindedness), reinforced by Titus' personal example of integrity, seriousness, and pure doctrine. Titus 2:6-7 (KJV) - "Young men likewise exhort to be sober minded. In all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity,"

question: In Titus 2:8, what type of speech must the Christian minister maintain, and what effect will it have on opponents?
opt1: Aggressive speech that humiliates adversaries; that critics may be driven out of the city in fear
opt2: Mystical speech cloaked in allegorical riddles; that philosophers may be bewildered by secret codes
opt3: Sound speech, that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you
opt4: Flattering speech pleasing to pagan rulers; that Roman magistrates may bestow gifts upon the church
correct: Sound speech, that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you
explanation: Irreproachable, wholesome communication disarms hostile critics, leaving them ashamed because they find nothing legitimate to slander. Titus 2:8 (KJV) - "Sound speech, that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you."

question: According to Titus 2:9-10, how should Christian bondservants conduct themselves toward their masters, and what exalted purpose does their faithfulness serve?
opt1: Defiant, demanding immediate emancipation, answering insolently, seizing property; that they may prove civil liberty
opt2: Silent, working only when watched, concealing masters' goods, plotting escape; that they may avoid labor
opt3: Flattering, seeking personal promotion over other slaves, sharing stolen food; that they may buy freedom
opt4: Obedient, pleasing well in all things, not answering again, not purloining, but shewing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour
correct: Obedient, pleasing well in all things, not answering again, not purloining, but shewing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour
explanation: Christian servants who display submissiveness, honesty, and trustworthiness make the gospel attractive, adorning and beautifying the doctrine of God our Saviour. Titus 2:9-10 (KJV) - "Exhort servants to be obedient unto their own masters, and to please them well in all things; not answering again; Not purloining, but shewing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things."

question: What universal, gracious revelation is declared in Titus 2:11 as the divine catalyst for holy living?
opt1: For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men
opt2: For the imperial decree of Rome granting universal citizenship has been signed
opt3: For the ancient wisdom of Greek philosophy has reached every island
opt4: For the ceremonial law of Moses has been made binding on all nations
correct: For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men
explanation: God's saving grace has broken into human history through the incarnation of Christ, bringing the offer of redemption to all classes and peoples. Titus 2:11 (KJV) - "For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men,"

question: According to Titus 2:12, what does the grace of God actively train and instruct believers to renounce and how to live in this present world?
opt1: Teaching us that indulging fleshly pleasures is harmless, and we should seek earthly luxury without guilt
opt2: Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world
opt3: Teaching us that observing ceremonial fasts is sufficient, and we should withdraw into physical seclusion
opt4: Teaching us that external moral conduct is irrelevant, and we should focus solely on mystical visions
correct: Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world
explanation: Saving grace is a transformative pedagogical power that instructs Christians to repudiate sin and live with self-mastery, integrity toward others, and devotion to God. Titus 2:12 (KJV) - "Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world;"

question: In Titus 2:13, what glorious eschatological expectancy is designated as the 'blessed hope' of the Christian church?
opt1: Anticipating the political emancipation of all Christian provinces by imperial decree
opt2: Waiting for an angel to reconstruct the physical temple of Solomon on Mount Moriah
opt3: Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ
opt4: Hoping to achieve earthly physical immortality through scientific wisdom in Greece
correct: Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ
explanation: The believer lives in joyful expectancy of the second coming, explicitly confessing Jesus Christ as 'the great God and our Saviour'. Titus 2:13 (KJV) - "Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ;"

question: According to Titus 2:14, why did Christ give Himself for us, and what kind of people did He purify unto Himself?
opt1: That he might grant us worldly political dominance, and make us an elite aristocracy of merchants
opt2: That he might excuse our ongoing sinful lifestyles, and make us an indifferent congregation
opt3: That he might enforce the Levitical priesthood, and make us ceremonial keepers of the sabbath
opt4: That he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works
correct: That he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works
explanation: Christ's substitutionary death aimed to liberate believers from all lawlessness and purify a prized, unique people passionately devoted to doing good. Titus 2:14 (KJV) - "Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works."

question: In Titus 3:1-2, what civic duties and interpersonal conduct does Paul instruct Titus to remind believers to maintain?
opt1: To be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work, to speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men
opt2: To incite public riots against Roman taxation, to defy magistrates, to speak evil of pagan rulers, to engage in armed resistance
opt3: To avoid all contact with civil authorities, to refuse to pay taxes, to live in isolated mountain communes
opt4: To demand political appointments in the municipal government, to litigate against neighbors in civil courts
correct: To be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work, to speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men
explanation: Believers are called to civic obedience, law-abiding citizenship, readiness for benevolent works, peacefulness, gentleness, and universal humility. Titus 3:1-2 (KJV) - "Put them in mind to be subject to principalities and powers, to obey magistrates, to be ready to every good work, To speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men."

question: According to Titus 3:3, how does Paul describe our unregenerate past life prior to experiencing the saving grace of God?
opt1: Righteous, morally enlightened, disciplined in virtue, loving our neighbors, and honoring God
opt2: Foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another
opt3: Wise philosophers who understood divine truth and practiced universal benevolence
opt4: Devout observers of Mosaic statutes who kept themselves unstained by pagan culture
correct: Foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another
explanation: Paul humbles human pride by recounting the universal past depravity of believers, enslaved to passions, malice, envy, and mutual hatred. Titus 3:3 (KJV) - "For we ourselves also were sometimes foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving divers lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another."

question: In the classic soteriological declaration of Titus 3:5, how are believers saved, and what is excluded as the basis of salvation?
opt1: By ceremonial sacrifices offered in the temple, according to human merit and ancestral heritage
opt2: By our strict observance of the ten commandments, through philosophical enlightenment and intellectual reason
opt3: Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost
opt4: By our baptismal credentials and monetary tithes, according to the decree of church councils
correct: Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost
explanation: Salvation is entirely unearned: human works of righteousness are completely excluded, and deliverance is bestowed solely by divine mercy through the Spirit's cleansing and renewal. Titus 3:5 (KJV) - "Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost;"

question: According to Titus 3:7, having been justified by God's grace, what glorious status and inheritance do believers receive?
opt1: That we should be made earthly kings possessing Roman provinces and physical armies
opt2: That we should be made immune to all physical sickness and temporal death in this world
opt3: That we should be granted exclusive commercial monopolies across the Mediterranean ports
opt4: That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life
correct: That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life
explanation: Justification by grace constitutes believers as true legal heirs of God, possessing the assured hope of eternal life. Titus 3:7 (KJV) - "That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life."

question: In Titus 3:8, what does Paul charge Titus to affirm constantly regarding those who have believed in God?
opt1: That they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men
opt2: That they which have believed in God should abandon manual trades and live on church charity
opt3: That they which have believed in God must avoid doing good works lest they rely on human merit
opt4: That they which have believed in God should debate endlessly about genealogies in public markets
correct: That they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men
explanation: Genuine saving faith must inevitably bear practical fruit: believers are solemnly charged to be diligent and intentional in maintaining good works. Titus 3:8 (KJV) - "This is a faithful saying, and these things I will that thou affirm constantly, that they which have believed in God might be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable unto men."

question: What theological distractions and disputations are believers commanded to avoid in Titus 3:9, and why?
opt1: Avoid preaching the gospel to Gentiles; for salvation is reserved exclusively for Israel
opt2: Avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain
opt3: Avoid reading the Old Testament scriptures; for ancient writings are obsolete
opt4: Avoid teaching sound doctrine to older men; for youth should remain silent
correct: Avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain
explanation: Paul forcefully commands avoidance of foolish speculations, mythic pedigrees, and legalistic controversies because they yield zero spiritual profit. Titus 3:9 (KJV) - "But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain."

question: According to Titus 3:10-11, how should church leadership handle a divisive, factious person (heretic)?
opt1: Appoint him as an elder immediately to appease his faction; knowing that titles produce harmony
opt2: Engage him in weekly public debates for several years; knowing that human logic will convince him
opt3: A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject; knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself
opt4: Report him to Roman civil authorities for execution; knowing that civil magistrates punish heresy
correct: A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject; knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself
explanation: A divisive sect-maker who persists after two formal biblical warnings must be rejected from church fellowship, having willfully condemned himself. Titus 3:10-11 (KJV) - "A man that is an heretick after the first and second admonition reject; Knowing that he that is such is subverted, and sinneth, being condemned of himself."

question: In Titus 3:12, where does Paul instruct Titus to meet him once Artemas or Tychicus arrives in Crete?
opt1: To Rome: for I have determined to face trial before Caesar
opt2: To Corinth: for I have determined to attend the Isthmian games
opt3: To Jerusalem: for I have determined to keep the feast of Pentecost
opt4: To Nicopolis: for I have determined there to winter
correct: To Nicopolis: for I have determined there to winter
explanation: Paul plans to spend the winter months in the coastal city of Nicopolis in Western Greece, summoning Titus to rejoin him there. Titus 3:12 (KJV) - "When I shall send Artemas unto thee, or Tychicus, be diligent to come unto me to Nicopolis: for I have determined there to winter."

question: Whom does Paul urge Titus to help diligently on their missionary journey in Titus 3:13 so that nothing is lacking unto them?
opt1: Zenas the lawyer and Apollos
opt2: Luke the physician and Demas
opt3: Barnabas the Levite and John Mark
opt4: Aquila and Priscilla
correct: Zenas the lawyer and Apollos
explanation: Titus is charged with practical pastoral hospitality, assisting Zenas the Christian lawyer and the eloquent teacher Apollos with traveling provisions. Titus 3:13 (KJV) - "Bring Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey diligently, that nothing be wanting unto them."

question: According to Titus 3:14, why must Christian believers learn to maintain good works for necessary uses?
opt1: That they may receive imperial pensions from Rome
opt2: That they be not unfruitful
opt3: That they may purchase exemptions from manual labor
opt4: That they may be praised by pagan Greek poets
correct: That they be not unfruitful
explanation: Paul's closing pastoral concern is that Christians cultivate practical, active benevolence to meet pressing human needs and live fruitful lives. Titus 3:14 (KJV) - "And let ours also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they be not unfruitful."
